items.title: CAR-T biotech Caribou makes ‘heartbreaking’ call to shrink headcount, halt pipeline
items.summary: The Bay Area biotech is discontinuing all clinical development activities and implementing a "substantial reduction in workforce."

items.title: Stryker strikes up a new CEO in Spencer Stiles as Kevin Lobo moves upstairs
items.summary: Stryker veteran Spencer Stiles will take up the chief executive role as its former CEO Kevin Lobo will move into the boardroom.

items.title: Big Pharma-backed Nuvig halts development of lead fusion protein in rare autoimmune disease
items.summary: Big Pharma-backed Nuvig Therapeutics has halted one of the two trials for its sole clinical asset after determining the program wouldn’t be able to advance quickly enough.

items.title: Abbott nabs FDA approval for new CardioMEMS HF System that allows heart readings to be seen at home
items.summary: Abbott has been given U.S. clearance for new updates to its CardioMEMS HF System that allow for patient-facing capabilities through its CardioGuide HF App.

items.title: Biotech’s peptide shows promise as ‘bait molecule’ to treat neuropathic pain in mice
items.summary: While psychedelic drugs may be capturing all the attention when it comes to finding fresh ways to treat neuropathic pain, research with mice has suggested a peptide approach may also be effective.

items.title: ArriVent’s phase 3 lung cancer trial flops, sinking stock
items.summary: A phase 3 lung cancer study of ArriVent BioPharma’s EGFR inhibitor has missed its primary endpoint, sending the biotech’s stock down 57% in early trading on the Nasdaq.

items.title: Kairos seizes moment to push prostate cancer prospect into earlier setting
items.summary: Kairos Pharma is moving prostate cancer prospect ENV-105 into an earlier line of treatment in response to midphase survival data.

items.title: Forbion’s ‘landmark’ €2.3B fundraise to benefit 30 ‘high potential’ biotechs
items.summary: Forbion has touted its “landmark” 2.3 billion euro ($2.6 billion) fundraise across two funds as a new record for the European life sciences-focused VC firm.

items.title: Pharma’s free lunches for clinicians bloat prescription bills: Cochrane review
items.summary: Promotional interactions between clinicians and pharmaceutical companies are probably associated with harmful outcomes, according to a Cochrane review that assessed free meals, ads and other dealings.

items.title: BMS fills out Zenbexus picture with post-approval PFS victory in multiple myeloma
items.summary: BMS has put up the progression-free survival numbers on its recently approved Zenbexus regimen, more than doubling the score over a control cocktail of daratumumab, bortezomib and dexamethasone.

items.title: Pfizer's Tukysa snags first-line approval in HER2+ breast cancer maintenance
items.summary: Pfizer bagged a coveted first-line maintenance approval for Tukysa. In combination with HER2 antibody drugs, the treatment can significantly delay disease progression for patients with advanced breast cancer.

items.title: Viatris to snap up Pacira's non-opioid pain pipeline for $1.65B
items.summary: In a push to up its investments in patent-protected medicines, Viatris is set to acquire Pacira BioSciences, including two high-margin non-opioid pain therapies.

items.title: Argenx walks away from Vyvgart Sjögren's disease trial after futility flag
items.summary: Just shy of two months after teeing up its FcRn blocker Vyvgart Hytrulo for entry into another potential immunology niche, argenx has stumbled in a late-stage trial testing the drug against a separate target.

items.title: CSL Seqirus blasted for ‘multiple and prolonged deficiencies’
items.summary: A U.K. drug marketing watchdog has slammed CSL Seqirus for “multiple and prolonged deficiencies” in its systems, governance and oversight.

items.title: Melissa explains it all in menopause team up with Bayer
items.summary: Bayer is teaming up with American actress and director Melissa Joan Hart to boost awareness about hot flashes treatment Lynkuet by tapping her personal experiences.

items.title: Theramex pays up to $250M for Asieris' novel cervical lesion treatment
items.summary: Should an EU approval go through, the deal allows Asieris to piggyback its global expansion on Theramex’s established women’s health infrastructure across Europe.

items.title: PhRMA launches new legal challenge as CMS brings 'most favored nation' pricing to Medicare Part B
items.summary: As the Trump administration advances plans to bring its “most favored nation” drug pricing model to Medicare Part B, the pharmaceutical industry’s top lobbying group is pushing back in court.

items.title: Sanofi drafts NY Knicks star Karl-Anthony Towns for COVID, Nuvaxovid awareness push
items.summary: New York Knicks champ Karl-Anthony Towns is sharing his personal experience with COVID to encourage others to talk with their doctors about vaccination options.

items.title: Novartis' Rhapsido tackles 2 most common forms of chronic hives with swift FDA expansion
items.summary: A little over a year after landing its flagship approval in chronic hives, Novartis’ oral BTK inhibitor Rhapsido is expanding its reach with a new FDA nod that comes with a notable ‘first’ for the field.

items.title: Halozyme stymies subcutaneous Keytruda launch in select European countries as Merck vows to fight patent claims
items.summary: After facing a setback in Germany late last year, Merck & Co.’s European marketing plans for its below-the-skin Keytruda SC are growing more complicated.

items.title: New API Innovation Center index spotlights supply chain stress points
items.summary: The National Fragility Index, launched by the API Innovation Center, warned that more than 550 million prescriptions filled in the U.S. in 2023 were categorized as being highly or severely vulnerable to supply chain interruptions.

items.title: How drugmakers are tapping into the GLP-1 frenzy's unprecedented 'consumer overlay'
items.summary: With the advent of powerful GLP-1 medications from Novo and Eli Lilly, the conversation about obesity as a chronic disease has begun to shift, along with the understanding of how tackling weight can trigger a multitude of downstream health benefits.

items.title: Scaling psychedelics comes with uncertainty ‘baked into the sauce’
items.summary: The possibility of psychedelic therapies for PTSD or treatment-resistant depression in the U.S. has never been greater. But even as the industry inches closer to an FDA go-ahead, the realities of approved psychedelic medicine are far from decided.

items.title: Catalent wins access to Iro and launches next-gen development platform
items.summary: Catalent will gain access to Ori's Iro platform, a proprietary automated cell and gene therapy manufacturing system that speeds up development and reduces costs.

items.title: Rising Stars: How VML Health’s Molly Kanofsky turns ‘an idea on a page’ into real-world impact
items.summary: VML Health's Molly Kanofsky ended up in the pharma marketing world after an unexpected career detour, where she's now able to merge her passion for healthcare with her creative side.

items.title: Noom puts a spooky voice to the haunting threat of weight regain for GLP-1 users in new spot
items.summary: Noom's horror movie-esque new ad showcases the haunting threat of weight regain on GLP-1s, which the Noom app can help fend off.

items.title: ViiV girds data package for Cabenuva in competitive HIV treatment market
items.summary: As competition in both the HIV treatment and prevention fields continues to mount, GSK’s ViiV Healthcare is looking to expand the reach of its long-acting Cabenuva, homing in on the combination treatment’s potential to help people whose infection isn’t adequately kept in check by antiretrovirals.

items.title: AbbVie, Genmab score first-line DLBCL win for Epkinly, teeing up challenge to Roche's Polivy
items.summary: Epkinly plus R-CHOP cut the risk of progression or death by 51% compared with R-CHOP alone in newly diagnosed DLBCL, setting up a potential first-line challenge to Roche’s Polivy.

items.title: Proposed nuclear safety rules threaten to stall Novartis’ Pluvicto expansion
items.summary: Novartis’ flagship radioligand therapy Pluvicto entered a rapid growth phase recently, driven by FDA approvals in earlier-stage prostate cancer and broader uptake in community settings. But a regulatory overhaul proposed by federal nuclear authorities now threatens to derail that momentum, potentially raising administrative hurdles that experts say could force clinics to rethink patient care while…

items.title: Genentech celebrates 50 years of 'The Impossible Bet' in anniversary documentary
items.summary: Known as the "original biotech," Genentech is unlocking its archives to shine light on its past, present and future in a new documentary celebrating its 50-year anniversary.

items.title: BD commits $19B amid US onshoring push, with $3B earmarked for manufacturing growth
items.summary: With a substantial multi-year investment in the offing, BD has joined a wave of healthcare companies upping their commitments to the U.S., this time focusing squarely on medical technology and the essential consumables used daily by doctors and patients.

items.title: Gilead partners with Calm to roll out disease-specific emotional wellness support
items.summary: Sleep app Calm is helping Gilead achieve its dream of helping its patients through a journey of whole-person health.

items.title: Shionogi strikes $2B deal for IntraBio hot off FDA label expansion
items.summary: The acquisition builds on Shionogi’s plans to diversify beyond its anti-infectious disease drug base and to beef up its budding rare disease unit.
